id: Traskforce! Ft. Eugene Wolfin-Rogue and Vagabond, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Traskforce! Ft. Eugene Wolfin
long_description:
Starring Eugene Wolfin on vocals, the octet will present a fizzing set of big band swing, Broadway hits, and gorgeous ballads. Hear the fine lyricism of the 20th century sung by one of Wellington’s most exciting performers.

Free entry! Koha encouraged.

For the last 8 years vocalist Eugene Wolfin has been a regular of Wellington music scene performing in a wide variety of genres including Jazz, Blues, and Rock ’n’ Roll. He has had a hand in a few local Musical Theatre productions performing lead roles in ‘Chess’ and the modern hit ‘If/Then', and is a regular in front of Jazz Orchestras including the Royal New Zealand Air Force Band and the Rodger Fox Big Band.

Traskforce! is bandleader Alex Trask’s most swinging musical organisation. They play fresh arrangements of original compositions, classic swing, and Broadway ballads. This includes songs from the Basie repertoire, Bob Mintzer, Oliver Nelson, Quincey Jones, and Lionel Bart's Oliver! to name a few. The five horn arrangements allow for the power of a big band and the subtlety of a quartet to shine side by side. The band is made up of Wellington’s top players, including members of the Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra, the RNZAF band, NZSM faculty, and rising stars.

Photo by Oscar Laven

id: Wellington Calling Open Mic-The Undercurrent, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Wellington Calling Open Mic
long_description:
The Undercurrent presents the Wellington Calling Open Mic!

The Undercurrent is hosting the Wellington Calling Open Mic and we're looking for diverse acts to contribute! Each performer gets the chance to have a six-minute set with a microphone, guitar and piano provided. This is an originals only event. We want to encourage new creative voices to be heard. “We want to provide a positive and encouraging environment for established and fledgling acts to shine in. It's a pretty inspiring place to perform,” says host Steven Hood.

Each performer will need to sign up in person before 7:30pm and registrations of interest need to be emailed to openwandw@gmail.com before August 27.

The feature act is Karim Efremov (aka Keey Fremm). His music explores the space between them—drawing inspiration from jazz improvisation, cinematic storytelling, heavy rock, classical traditions, and the unexpected. His work is driven by curiosity, theatricality, and a desire to challenge conventional musical expectations.

Bizarre-Esque is the live performance project through which these ideas come to life. More than a band, it is an evolving musical experience that embraces contrast, experimentation, and storytelling, inviting audiences into a world where familiar sounds are continually reimagined. For this performance, Karim will present a selection of his original compositions, joined by Sylvester Green (trumpet), whose musicianship brings an exciting collaborative dimension to the music.

Thursday August 27
Doors 7pm
Music 7:30pm
Koha entry

Snacks, a range of refreshing drinks, tea & coffee, and of course...books available for purchase!

We’ll see you there ☆

id: Cuba St Tavern Presents: Cian O'Donnell-Cuba St Tavern, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Cuba St Tavern Presents: Cian O'Donnell
long_description:
CUBA ST TAVERN PRESENTS: WINTER SERIES

Next up: Cian

Friday 28 August | Doors 7pm

The Winter Series rolls on, and this round we're pulling in a genuine legend of New Zealand music culture: DJ, broadcaster, record shop owner, promoter and traveller Cian O'Donnell, who's been playing quality tunes for local ears since the late 1980s. Come get your Friday knock-off drink on with him behind the decks.

Born in Hereford, England, O'Donnell's path to music was a familiar one—until landing in Wainuiomata in 1987 turned it into a life's work, and New Zealand into home. Since then, DJ Cian has earned a Gilles Peterson-style reputation for digging up the good stuff through his DJ sets and radio shows, his long-running Auckland club night The Turnaround, and behind the counter of the record shops he's called home, most famously Conch Records on Ponsonby Road.

Owner of one of Aotearoa's deepest record collections, Cian has built a reputation for sets that move effortlessly across genres. Whether he's playing to a packed dancefloor or a room full of mates, it's always about the next record - the one you didn't know you needed to hear.

Joining him is Jewel School, warming things up before Cian takes over for the evening.

Immersive lighting from @lighterxx, with sound powered by a custom Tubs Audio system.

Friday 28 August
Doors 7pm
Cuba St Tavern

id: Never Mind The Rowlocks, Here's The Wellington Sea Shanty Society EP-Abandoned Taproom Petone, Petone, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Never Mind The Rowlocks, Here's The Wellington Sea Shanty Society EP
long_description:
The wave doesn’t conform to the shape of the rock. It smashes it. The sea doesn’t pretend to be hospitable. It summons courage. And a shantyband never licks the captain's boot. They release another EP!

The best shanties invite us to open our hearts along with the bottle. To draw strength from camaraderie and drown our pettinesses. To seek the rough edge of the wave and savour the salt within. And so, the WSSS have issued a call to arms with their new collection: Never Mind the Rowlocks, Here’s the Wellington Sea Shanty Society.

Never fear if you find yourself adrift on a sea of AI slop, lapping at your hull, lulling you to sleep — Lake Davineer, Vorn dont Le Père Était Marin, Young Nic, Tomas el Largo, and Louis Quatorze are back again to fill your sails and slap the codfish slime clean off your cheeks.

Just when everyone is lamenting the empty galleys of the good ship Wellington, and those ol’ scurvy-mongers are promising renewed bounty if you would only tack five degrees to port or starboard come election time, these songs remind us the sea at least will sustain us, and there’s rum and (metaphorical) guns for them that wants to fight.

Lin Seal | Wellington Nautical History Monthly

⚓⚓⚓

The scuttlebutt is true...⛵

The most seaworthy sea shanty band in the South Pacific is releasing their long-awaited 4th collection of new and old maritime bangers:
'Never Mind the Rowlocks - Here's the Wellington Sea Shanty Society'.

All aboard as we set sail for the salty horizon. Prepare to be battered once again by the 4-sailor squall of pure shanty.

Singalong shanties! Nautical games! Best dressed prizes!

Limited tickets.

Standing show (Seating reserved for those who need it: bookings@wellingtonseashantysociety.com).

⚓⚓⚓

WELLINGTON SEA SHANTY SOCIETY

Aotearoa New Zealand's Most 'Sea Worthy' Shanty Group™ have been belting out traditional and original sea songs from Aotearoa, France, Spain, the UK and more, since time immemorial (2012).
The W.S.S.S have toured Aotearoa and France multiple times and are known for their rowdy and participatory live shows. They've performed at Paimpol (one of the world's largest shanty festivals), Splore, Albany Folk Festival (Aus), Quebec Sea Shanty Festival (Canada) and a shipload of other festivals in NZ, France & Canada.

They will be playing new classics from their forthcoming EP 'Never Mind the Rowlocks' as well as your foamy favourites from the 'Sea Shanties of the 70s, 80s, & Today!' EP and their 'Now That's What I Call Sea Shanties' series.

id: The Temple (EP Release) And March Of The Kororā-Pyramid Club, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: The Temple (EP Release) And March Of The Kororā
long_description:
Pōneke's inimitable live ambient outfit The Temple returns to Pyramid Club to celebrate the release of their new EP VVV. The band will play the EP in full, then serve up a smorgasbord of deep-dish ambient soundscapes with a side of uplifting vibes.

A celebration, a sound bath, a deep listening ritual, a sanctum of presence. Vastness Vastness Vastness.

The Temple is Peter Liley (sax), Nathan Carter (percussion), and Jack Woodbury (electronics). These templars create hypnotic live-ambient soundscapes, drawing inspiration from underground, new age, sound art, and electronic music scenes. With The Temple as guides, ordinary places are transformed into spaces of deep presence and contemplation.
-
March of the Kororā are a pair of multi-instrumentalists trying to make sense of ecological collapse, injustice and resistance. Their first album, 'lonely blue penguin on a little blue planet', is born out of jazz jams, space explorations and rage.

name: Chutney
long_description:
The Undercurrent presents Chutney!

CHUTNEY is Australia’s leading klezmer fusion band. They draw on their Eastern European and Middle Eastern heritage to play a spicy mix of original bangers and fresh takes on infectious dance tunes. Led by the unbridled virtuosity of the duelling violin and clarinet, the band hopscotches from folk to pop, jazz to tango, classical to funk, east to west. 

CHUTNEY has taken the world music scene by storm, with their debut album Ajar, which won a triple Triple Gold Medal at the Global Music Awards. This is CHUTNEY’s New Zealand debut, and a night of passion, whimsy and high energy not to be missed!

id: Never Mind The Rowlocks, Here's The Wellington Sea Shanty Society EP-Raumati South Memorial Hall, Raumati, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Never Mind The Rowlocks, Here's The Wellington Sea Shanty Society EP
venue: Raumati South Memorial Hall, Raumati, Wellington
long_description:
The scuttlebutt is true...⛵

The most seaworthy sea shanty band in the South Pacific is releasing their long-awaited 4th collection of new and old maritime bangers:
'Never Mind the Rowlocks - Here's the Wellington Sea Shanty Society'.

All aboard as we set sail for the salty horizon. Prepare to be battered once again by the 4-sailor squall of pure shanty.

SINGALONG SHANTIES! NAUTICAL GAMES! BEST DRESSED PRIZES!

Standing show (email bookings@wellingtonseashantysociety.com if you need seating).

⚓⚓⚓

LIVE REVIEW - theatreview.org.nz

Having been handed a booklet of lyrics... we grab seats around the edge ... It’s all very casual, with the added delight of people dressed as sailors in striped tops and white hats, pirate hats and newspaper hats, and even life jackets! It’s like they know what is about to happen!

As the band takes to the stage... a spotlight falls upon storyteller Louis Tait. Microphone in hand he starts to weave a tale of the sea, to riffs of music from the band.

Back to those booklets of lyrics – this whole show is a singalong and it is with great enthusiasm that the first shanty begins...the audience sings and stomps and laughs.

It’s hard to describe the impact of stadium concert level audience euphoria in a small community hall, yet that is what it is. Bopping bodies, bathed in coloured light, so into the music, which is just fantastic in every way. The dance area is more like an ecstatic mosh pit.

What is it about shanties? They came out of shared singing and so they lend themselves to this, I guess. But what Vorn Dont le Père Etait Marin and Lake Davineer bring to these songs is a thoroughly modern, old-fashioned sense of fun and magic.

I am reserving specific comment for the currently most famous shanty in their repertoire, ‘The Wellerman’... The crowd goes wild! The stomping probably puts the hall onto Geonet. I would not have been surprised if a giant cracken had appeared and body-surfed the crowd.

⚓⚓⚓

WELLINGTON SEA SHANTY SOCIETY

Aotearoa New Zealand's Most 'Sea Worthy' Shanty Group™ have been belting out traditional and original sea songs from Aotearoa, France, Spain, the UK and more, since time immemorial (2012).

The W.S.S.S have toured Aotearoa and France multiple times and are known for their rowdy and participatory live shows. They've performed at Paimpol (one of the world's largest shanty festivals), Splore, Albany Folk Festival (Aus), Quebec Sea Shanty Festival (Canada) and a shipload of other festivals in NZ, France & Canada.

They will be playing new classics from their forthcoming EP 'Never Mind the Rowlocks' as well as your foamy favourites from the 'Sea Shanties of the 70s, 80s, & Today!' EP and their 'Now That's What I Call Sea Shanties' series.

id: Blair Morgan And Luca Joass-The Undercurrent, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Blair Morgan And Luca Joass
long_description:
The Undercurrent presents Blair Morgan & Luca Joass!

Ōtautahi singer-songwriter Blair Morgan brings his original songs to Wellington for a special afternoon performance. Blair's recently released album Sunday River blends folk, Americana and indie influences, telling stories of people, places and journeys. His songs travel from the streets of Lisbon to the west coast of Te Waipounamu, exploring themes of resilience, friendship and home through warm acoustic performances, and engaging storytelling. Performing solo, Blair presents the songs as they were first written- just voice, guitar, harmonica and the stories behind them.

Joining Blair is Wellington singer-songwriter Luca Joass. Known for his heartfelt songwriting and engaging live performances, Luca released his debut single “Young & Free” last year, accompanied by a beautifully crafted music video. As co-founder of Neato Productions, he has also directed several music videos for Blair's Sunday River album.

Come along for an afternoon of original New Zealand songwriting in one of Wellington's most welcoming listening rooms.

Saturday August 29
Doors 3pm
Music 3:30pm
$20

Tickets available online and at the door!

Snacks, a range of refreshing drinks, tea & coffee, and of course...books available for purchase!

We’ll see you there ☆
